extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent applicants, attorneys, and agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners (and practitioners) on Office actions, citation practices, provision of cited references, and procedural requirements during examination and reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes that the record of the prosecution as a whole does not make clear his or her reasons for allowing a claim or claims, the examiner may set forth such reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reasons shall be incorporated into an Office action rejecting other claims or be the subject of a separate communication to the applicant or patent owner. The applicant/patent owner may file a statement commenting on the reasons for allowance within such time as specified by the examiner. Failure by the examiner to respond to any such statement does not give rise to any implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Action Summary (PTOL-326) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the first action procedure the examiner signifies on form PTOL-326 certain information including the period set for reply, any attachments, and a 'Summary of Action' which is the position taken on all the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office Action Summary form PTOL-326 serves as the first page of the Office action (though a PTOL-90 may be used as a coversheet) and will identify any allowed claims. Attachments have the same paper number and are considered part of the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone discussions after first action
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner may indicate that a discussion with applicant’s or patent owner’s representative may result in agreements whereby the application (or patent under reexamination) may be placed in condition for allowance and that the examiner will telephone the representative within about 2 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such practice allows the representative to be prepared. Any resulting amendment may be made by the applicant’s/patent owner’s attorney or agent or by the examiner as an examiner’s amendment. When extensive amendments are necessary, it is preferable that they be filed by the attorney/agent to reduce Office workload and to provide the file wrapper with a better record including applicant’s arguments per 37 CFR 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required identification on replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to Office actions should include the application number as well as the 4-digit art unit number and the examiner’s name to expedite handling within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to include the 4-digit confirmation number on every paper filed. See MPEP § 503 for explanation of the confirmation number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory notification of rejections (35 U.S.C. 132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever, on examination, any claim is rejected or any objection made, notification of the reasons for rejection and/or objection together with such information and references as may be useful in judging the propriety of continuing the prosecution should be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When necessary, include particular figure(s), page(s), paragraph(s) of the references, and brief relevant comments. For rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103, set out the way a reference is modified or how plural references are combined. Exceptional cases and pro se inventors may require more complete explanation (see 37 CFR 1.104(c)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of concluding form paragraphs (7.100, 7.101, 7.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of form paragraphs 7.100, 7.101, or 7.102 should conclude all actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These paragraphs provide templates for contact information (name, phone, duty days/hours, supervisor contact). Specific bracketed fields must be filled with examiner name, phone, normal duty hours, days worked, supervisor name and number, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner responsibilities for new assistants
rubrics_metrics.description: After the search has been completed, action is taken in light of the references found; the primary examiner must thoroughly review applications handled by assistant examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistant should explain the invention and pertinent references; the primary may indicate action (restriction/election or merits), how references are to be applied in rejections, or authorize allowance if claims are not met by references and no further field of search is known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory review for 3rd-action and 5-year pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisory patent examiners should personally check pendency of every application up for the third or subsequent Office action and applications pending five years should be carefully studied with every effort made to terminate prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications pending five years are to be considered 'special' by the examiner to accomplish termination of prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation data requirements (37 CFR 1.104(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: When domestic patents, patent application publications, or foreign patents are cited, specific identifying data must be stated (numbers, dates, names; publication numbers/dates; country and patentee names, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only part of a foreign document is involved, identify particular pages and sheets. If printed publications are cited provide author (if any), title, date, pages or plates, and place of publication or place where a copy can be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits for rejections based on Office personal knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rejection is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an employee of the Office, the data shall be as specific as possible and the reference must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an affidavit shall be subject to contradiction or explanation by the affidavits of the applicant and other persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite pertinent prior art and explain relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: During examination, the examiner should cite appropriate prior art which is nearest to the subject matter defined in the claims and when such prior art is cited, its pertinence should be explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must consider all prior art references (alone and in combination) cited in the application or reexamination, including those in a properly submitted Information Disclosure Statement (see MPEP § 609). Form paragraph 7.96 may be used as an introductory sentence; relevance should be explained in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of cited references furnished to applicant — general rule and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of cited foreign patent documents and non-patent literature references (except noted exceptions) are automatically furnished without charge to applicant together with the Office action in which they are cited; copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications are not provided in paper to applicants and are not placed in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of references cited by examiner are provided to applicant except where the documents: (A) are cited by applicant in accordance with MPEP § 609, § 707.05(b), and § 708.02; (B) have been referred to in applicant’s disclosure statement; (C) are cited and have been provided in a parent application; (D) are cited by a third party in a submission under 37 CFR 1.99; or (E) are U.S. Patents or U.S. application publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include prior art on allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed applications should generally contain a citation of pertinent prior art for printing in the patent, even if no claim presented during prosecution was considered unpatentable over such prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only if a proper search has not revealed any relevant prior art is it appropriate to send an application to issue with no art cited. In that case the examiner must write 'None' on form PTO-892 and insert it in the file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review parent applications for continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: In all continuation and continuation-in-part applications, the parent applications should be reviewed for pertinent prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where references have been cited during prosecution of parent applications and a continuing application with no newly cited references is ready for allowance, the cited references of the parent should be listed on form PTO-892 and placed in the continuing application's file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of international search report citations (PCT) by applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and/or their attorneys in PCT-related national applications may wish to cite the material citations from the PCT International Search Report by an Information Disclosure Statement under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 to ensure consideration by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documents from the International Search Report are not provided in copy or English translation, the examiner may exercise discretion whether to obtain the copy/translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: When examiner should obtain copies/translations
rubrics_metrics.description: In instances where no IDS has been filed and documents are cited in the International Search Report but neither a copy nor an English translation (or English family member) is provided, the examiner may exercise discretion in deciding whether to obtain copies/translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of documents cited will be provided as set forth in MPEP § 707.05(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedures to provide copies and record citations
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist in providing copies of references or access, the examiner should type the citation on form PTO-892 (using OACS), place the PTO-892 in front of the file wrapper, include in the file wrapper all references cited by the examiner which are to be furnished to the applicant, and turn the application in to technical support for counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any application handed in without all required references will be returned to the examiner; missing references should be obtained and the file returned promptly. For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing see IFW Manual section 3.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to obtain U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications (E-Patent Reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications are available via the USPTO web site and the E-Patent Reference feature of Private PAIR; in June 2004 USPTO ceased mailing paper copies of cited U.S. patents and publications with Office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to Private PAIR is required to use E-Patent Reference. Practitioners and unrepresented applicants are urged to: (1) obtain a PKI digital certificate, (2) obtain a USPTO customer number, (3) associate customer number with correspondence addresses, (4) install electronic filing software, and (5) ensure Internet access (high-speed recommended). E-Patent Reference allows selecting and downloading cited references as complete PDFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-submitted citations do not replace examiner search obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted citations will not in any way diminish the obligation of examiners to conduct independent prior art searches, or relieve examiners of citing other pertinent prior art of which they may be aware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art submitted by applicant in the manner provided in MPEP § 609 will not be supplied with an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of listing references on PTO-892
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing references for the first time, identifying data should be placed on form PTO-892 'Notice of References Cited' which will be attached to the Office action; no distinction is to be made between references on which a claim is rejected and those formerly referred to as 'pertinent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With the exception of applicant-submitted citations, where an applicant in an amendatory paper refers to a reference that is subsequently relied upon by the examiner, such reference shall be cited by the examiner using form PTO-892 unless applicant has listed the reference on a form PTO-1449 or PTO/SB/08 initialed by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data to include for U.S. patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a U.S. patent application publication is cited, include the publication number, publication date, name of the applicant, class, and subclass; for U.S. patents include patent number, patent date, name of patentee, class and subclass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are encouraged to cite kind codes printed on U.S. publications and patents. Defensive Publications and Statutory Invention Registrations (SIRs) should be cited under 'U.S. Patent Documents.' See MPEP § 901.04 for kind codes and series details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data to include for foreign patents and published applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing foreign patents include patent number, kind code, citation date, name of the country, name of the patentee, and U.S. class/subclass if appropriate; for partial reliance specify sheet and page numbers and total sheets/pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign patents searched in Technology Centers filing by IPC should be cited using the appropriate IPC subclass/group/subgroup (cite classification on file wrapper 'Searched' box and PTO-892). If entire disclosure is relied on, total sheets/pages need not be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data to include for publications / non-patent literature (NPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts, abbreviatures, Alien Property Custodian publications, withdrawn U.S. patents, and other non-patent documents should be cited under 'Non-Patent Documents' on PTO-892 with sufficient information to determine identity and facilitate location of the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For books include author, title, date, pages relied on and STIC call number if available. For periodicals include author(s), article title, periodical title, volume, issue, date, and pages. Minimal citations (author, title, date) allowed only if complete bibliographic details are unknown or unavailable. Examples of accepted formats are provided in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not abbreviate titles; provide retrievable bibliographic info
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of books and periodicals SHOULD NOT be abbreviated such that identification is hindered; bibliographic information must be at least enough to identify the publication (author, title, date; for periodicals title, volume, date, pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimal citations may be used only if complete bibliographic details are unknown or unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite nonpatent references with document identification number properly
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a nonpatent literature reference has a document identification number, that number and the class and subclass should be included on PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format: (S00840001) Winslow, C.E.A. Fresh Air and Ventilation N.Y., E.P. Dutton, 1926, p. 97-112, TH 7653, W5, 315/22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain photocopies if original publications are outside the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original publication is located outside the Office the examiner should immediately make or order a photocopy of at least the portion relied upon and indicate the class and subclass in which it will be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the portion relied upon is placed in the file and classified appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format for electronic documents (WIPO ST.14 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: An electronic document citation should follow the WIPO ST.14 recommendation: use a format similar to paper documents with additional information: (A) the type of electronic medium in square brackets after the title (e.g., [online], [CD-ROM]); (B) the retrieval date in square brackets after publication date; (C) identification of the source with 'Retrieved from' and address; (D) indication of specific passages if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office copies of electronic documents must be retained if the same document may not be available in the future. If an electronic document is also available in paper form it need not be identified as electronic unless desirable. Numerous online-database and Internet examples are provided (e.g., World Patents Index, Medline, INSPEC).
